Marissa Cole: Heads up: we just shipped the first cut of **Route Experiments (route-level A/B testing)** in Console → Rollouts. This is an internal announce + enablement notes before we invite more beta accounts.

What it is:
• Define an experiment on a **route/endpoint** (A/B/n), deterministic assignment, configurable traffic splits.
• First-class metrics attribution by `{route, experiment_id, variant}` in Console: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, throughput, and cost/token.
• Guardrails: configure thresholds + alerts; initial behavior is **soft-stop** (mark degraded + notify). Optional hard-stop is available but gated (see below).

Enablement (internal):
• Feature flag: `route_experiments` (Console + APIs). Default OFF except allowlisted accounts.
• To enable for an internal/test account: file INT ticket (template: INT-1193) or ping #eng-releases with account_id + region.

Links (stubs, will fill in as docs finalize):
• PRD: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/route-experiments-prd (internal)
• How-to: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/route-experiments-operator-howto
• Dashboards: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/route-experiments-guardrails
• Runbook (assignment debugging): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/experiment-assignment-debug

Callouts:
• For best determinism/less skew: pass a stable stickiness key (`x-redwood-sticky-key`) or customer_id if you’re testing via the gateway.
• Console will show assigned variant; API also returns headers (details in docs).

Please reply here with questions / “I want to try this” + which route you want to test. :thumbsup:

Dylan Brooks: +1. If you’re dogfooding, start with a low blast radius route and do staged ramps (1% → 10% → 50%). We saw the most confusion when people jumped straight to 50/50 on high QPS.

RedwoodBot: Marissa Cole added a bookmark: "Route Experiments" (internal)

Connor O'Brien: Release note for internal train is going out later today. If your team wants this in the next sandbox refresh, please post in #eng-releases with “route experiments enablement” and we’ll coordinate flags per region.

Logan Wright: Telemetry note: attribution shows up in OTel spans as `redwood.experiment_id` + `redwood.variant_id`. If you’re doing custom dashboards, please avoid adding extra dimensions (region+model+route+variant can get spicy). We’ve already restricted tags on some high-cardinality metrics.

Sean Gallagher: SRE notes:
• Guardrail alerts are live (latency regression, error rate, attribution drop rate, propagation lag).
• Soft-stop is the default. Hard-stop exists but there’s a kill switch and we’re being conservative until we get more signal (false positives are a real concern).
• If you see “results stale” in Console, check propagation lag first.

Tessa Morgan: UX heads up: the creation flow is behind the same flag, and we’re iterating on copy around “stop” semantics (immediate vs drain). If anything reads weird, drop screenshots in #design.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC: if you can’t see the “Create experiment” button, it’s almost always role-based. For now, `Rollouts Admin` can create/start/stop, `Rollouts Viewer` is read-only. If you need a role updated, DM me + your org + desired role.

Rafael Mendes: For oncall/triage: the quickest way to debug assignment weirdness is the internal debug endpoint (RBAC’d). It returns the hash inputs + selected variant + config version. Please don’t paste raw customer identifiers into public channels; redact before sharing.

Marissa Cole: Adding one more note since a couple folks pinged me: yes, experiments apply **before fallback policy evaluation** (so you’re actually comparing variants, not accidentally falling back to the same thing). If you find a case where fallback overrides the variant, that’s a bug — please file it + link the route.

Dylan Brooks: Also: if you run streaming, make sure you’re on latest router build. We had a beta issue where attribution could drop on retries; fixed in the last patch.

Connor O'Brien: Office hours: Thu 2pm PT for anyone wanting help setting up a first experiment. I’ll post the calendar link once it’s created.

Marissa Cole: Thanks all. Keep feedback coming — especially around (1) stickiness key guidance and (2) whether the results dashboard tells the story clearly without a stats-sig engine. That’s explicitly out of GA scope but we want the deltas/guardrails to be unambiguous.
